Qatar’s Al Waha Energy Launches $2.2 Billion Gas Expansion

Qatar’s oil and gas sector is set for further growth as Al Waha Energy, a leading domestic producer, announced a $2.2 billion investment to expand its natural gas production capacity. The project, centered on the Ras Laffan Industrial City, aims to increase Al Waha’s annual output by 12% over the next three years, responding to rising global demand for liquefied natural gas (LNG).

The expansion includes the construction of two new gas processing trains and the upgrade of existing infrastructure, with completion targeted for late 2027. Al Waha Energy CEO Khalifa Al-Naimi described the move as “a strategic step to reinforce Qatar’s position as a reliable energy exporter,” adding that “the investment will create hundreds of local jobs and support the country’s long-term economic diversification goals.”

Industry analysts have welcomed the announcement. “This expansion underscores Qatar’s commitment to maintaining its competitive edge in LNG exports,” said Mariam Al Suwaidi, senior analyst at the Gulf Energy Forum. “With Asian and European markets seeking stable energy supplies, Qatar’s increased capacity will be well-placed to capture additional market share.”

The Qatar Petroleum Association noted that the project aligns with national development plans and supports the state’s Vision 2030 economic strategy. Local suppliers are expected to benefit from procurement contracts, according to the Qatar Chamber of Commerce.

Al Waha Energy confirmed it will adhere to international environmental standards during the expansion, including enhanced emissions monitoring. The company said it is exploring partnerships with global technology providers to deploy carbon capture solutions as part of the new facilities.
